title: Native causal reasoning in neural models
bottleneck: Today's models excel at statistical correlation but cannot perform native interventional or counterfactual reasoning — asking what would happen if X changed, grounded in a structured model of cause and effect. Chain-of-thought can mimic causal language, yet models fail when causal structure differs from training correlations and cannot reliably distinguish confounders from true causes. No mainstream architecture has causal inference as a first-class primitive rather than an emergent accident.
why_it_blocks: Medicine, policy, and engineering all require causal answers. A model that confuses correlation with causation gives confidently wrong recommendations in exactly the high-stakes settings where AI is most wanted.
current_state: Researchers graft causal graphs and do-calculus prompts onto LLMs, and lab evaluations report only about 60% reliability on causal inference tasks. True causal world models remain an open research frontier.
